narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The sacred writer: narration and the words that introduce speech.

sarah.name: Sara
sarah.note: Abraham's wife; laughing with joy at Isaac's birth, then hard and peremptory about Agar.

the-lord.name: The Lord
the-lord.note: God speaking to Abraham; reassuring, sovereign.

hagar.name: Agar
hagar.note: Sara's Egyptian bondwoman, cast out; despairing in the wilderness.

angel.name: Angel of the Lord
angel.note: The angel of God calling to Agar from heaven; consoling, speaking in God's name.

abimelech.name: Abimelech
abimelech.note: King of Gerara, speaking with his general Phicol beside him; courteous, seeking an oath.

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.note: The patriarch, a hundred years old; grieved over Ismael, then firm and plain in dealing with Abimelech.

1.t: And the Lord visited Sara, as he had promised: and fulfilled what he had spoken.

2.t: And she conceived and bore a son in her old age, at the time that God had foretold her.

3.t: And Abraham called the name of his son, whom Sara bore him, Isaac.

4.t: And he circumcised him the eighth day, as God had commanded him,

5.t: When he was a hundred years old: for at this age of his father, was Isaac born.

6.t: God hath made a laughter for me: whosoever shall hear of it will laugh with me.

7.t: Who would believe that Abraham should hear that Sara gave suck to a son, whom she bore to him in his old age?

8.t: And the child grew, and was weaned: and Abraham made a great feast on the day of his weaning.

9.t: And when Sara had seen the son of Agar, the Egyptian, playing with Isaac, her son, she said to Abraham:

10.t: Cast out this bondwoman and her son; for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with my son Isaac.

11.t: Abraham took this grievously for his son.

12.t: Let it not seem grievous to thee for the boy, and for thy bondwoman: in all that Sara hath said to thee, hearken to her voice: for in Isaac shall thy seed be called.

13.t: But I will make the son also of the bondwoman a great nation, because he is thy seed.

14.t: So Abraham rose up in the morning, and taking bread and a bottle of water, put it upon her shoulder, and delivered the boy, and sent her away. And she departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Bersabee.

15.t: And when the water in the bottle was spent, she cast the boy under one of the trees that were there.

16.t: And she went her way, and sat over against him a great way off, as far as a bow can carry, for she said:
I will not see the boy die:
and sitting over against, she lifted up her voice and wept.

17.t: And God heard the voice of the boy: and an angel of God called to Agar from heaven, saying:
What art thou doing, Agar? fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the boy, from the place wherein he is.

18.t: Arise, take up the boy, and hold him by the hand, for I will make him a great nation.
18.q: the angel speaks in God's person ("I will make him a great nation"); kept with the angel who is the named speaker

19.t: And God opened her eyes: and she saw a well of water, and went and filled the bottle, and gave the boy to drink.

20.t: And God was with him: and he grew, and dwelt in the wilderness, and became a young man, an archer.

21.t: And he dwelt in the wilderness of Pharan, and his mother took a wife for him out of the land of Egypt.

22.t: At the same time Abimelech, and Phicol the general of his army, said to Abraham:
God is with thee in all that thou dost.
22.q: said by Abimelech and Phicol together; the request is in the singular ("hurt me"), so given to Abimelech alone

23.t: Swear therefore by God, that thou wilt not hurt me, nor my posterity, nor my stock: but according to the kindness that I have done to thee, thou shalt do to me, and to the land wherein thou hast lived a stranger.

25.t: And he reproved Abimelech for a well of water, which his servants had taken away by force.

26.t: I knew not who did this thing: and thou didst not tell me, and I heard not of it till today.

27.t: Then Abraham took sheep and oxen, and gave them to Abimelech: and both of them made a league.

28.t: And Abraham set apart seven ewelambs of the flock.

29.t: What mean these seven ewelambs which thou hast set apart?

30.t: Thou shalt take seven ewelambs at my hand: that they may be a testimony for me, that I dug this well.

31.t: Therefore that place was called Bersabee; because there both of them did swear.

32.t: And they made a league for the well of oath.

33.t: And Abimelech and Phicol, the general of his army, arose and returned to the land of the Palestines. But Abraham planted a grove in Bersabee, and there called upon the name of the Lord God eternal.

34.t: And he was a sojourner in the land of the Palestines many days.
